source.title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let b be a vector field with bounded variation in the spatial variables. Can the theory of flows associated to weakly differentiable vector fields be extended to such BV fields under the assumption that the continuity equation with initial density 1 at time t = 0 admits a bounded solution rho_t?

evidence.quote: One of the open problems is to extend the theory to BV fields b, namely such that the continuity equation starting from 1 at t = 0 has a bounded solution rho_t.

accepted.question_text: Suppose the regular Lagrangian flow X(t,x) of a Sobolev vector field admits a first-order expansion in the differentiability-in-measure sense, so that for small r one has X(t, x + r y) = X(t, x) + r A(t, x) y plus an error that tends to 0 locally in measure. What is the nature of the matrix-valued map A(t,x) that appears in this expansion?

evidence.quote: This result raises in a natural way the following questions: What is the nature of A?
in turn, differentiability in measure is equivalent to |f(x+ry)-f(x)-rA(x)y|/r -> 0 locally in measure as r downarrow 0, for all y in R^n, for some matrix-valued local map A(x).

accepted.question_text: For the regular Lagrangian flow associated to a weakly differentiable vector field, where differentiability in measure has been proved in the Sobolev case, is this differentiability-in-measure property related to other weak differentiability notions, in particular approximate differentiability?

evidence.quote: Are there relations with other weak differentiability properties, as for instance the approximate differentiability (a concept deeply investigated in [20])?

accepted.question_text: In the Sobolev setting for weakly differentiable vector fields, can the differentiability-in-measure estimate for the associated regular Lagrangian flow be strengthened to yield some measure-theoretic form of local Lipschitz regularity of the flow?
accepted.context_brief: Local Lipschitz regularity from differentiability in measure

evidence.quote: Can we infer from (9), as it happens for approximate differentiability, some kind of 'local Lipschitz' regularity of the flow?

This result shows that, at least in the W^{1,p} case, with p > 1, 'local' Lipschitz regularity of the flow holds. Here 'local' should not be understood in the topological sense but, rather, in the measure-theoretic sense.

accepted.question_text: Can the differentiability-in-measure and related regularity results for the regular Lagrangian flow, proved in the Sobolev regime W^{1,p} with p > 1, be extended all the way down to the borderline cases W^{1,1} or BV for the underlying vector field?
accepted.context_brief: Borderline extension to W1,1 or BV

evidence.quote: For this reason we presently don't know whether these results can be extended up to the W^{1,1} or the BV case.

evidence.quote: This provides us with a sort of weak solution for (1), and it is still an open problem how the Eulerian form could be recovered.
